claims.text: The starting additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a homogeneous FCC matrix.
The starting alloy has a uniform elemental distribution.
Elevated-temperature degradation is governed by sequential formation of a biphasic oxide scale.
Selective oxidation of Cr initially forms a protective oxide layer.
Selective oxidation of Al initially forms a protective oxide layer.
The initial Cr/Al-rich oxide is fine, adherent, and retards degradation.
The initial protective oxide maintains the integrity of the FCC matrix.
Sustained exposure drives Ti diffusion toward the oxide/alloy interface or surface.
Diffusing Ti produces a secondary Ti-rich oxide.
The secondary Ti-rich oxide is less coherent or less adherent than the initial Cr/Al-rich oxide.
Formation of the Ti-rich oxide introduces interfacial stresses and microcracks.
Ti-rich oxide formation promotes scale spallation and accelerates degradation.
The layered-oxide degradation mechanism is more pronounced in oxidizing environments.
Under reducing conditions, lower oxygen potential limits formation of the protective Cr/Al-rich scale.
Reducing conditions lead to localized oxidation, including oxidation along grain boundaries.
Reducing conditions do not produce the pronounced duplex Cr/Al-rich and Ti-rich oxide structure predicted for oxidizing conditions.
The emergence of the Ti-rich layer under oxidizing conditions correlates with increased surface microcracking and fatigue degradation.
Reducing-atmosphere exposure produces less scale spallation than oxidizing-atmosphere exposure.
Exposure near 800°C for at least 100 hours is sufficient for significant surface diffusion and oxide-layer evolution.
Prior oxidation studies on related systems support protective roles for Cr and Al and a detrimental role for Ti diffusion.

contradictions.description: The Ti-rich oxide is placed inconsistently: the hypothesis associates its formation with the oxide/alloy interface, whereas the structural mediator calls it an outer layer and the mechanism describes Ti diffusion to the surface.
